from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite: Linear Transformations as Space Warping",
            [
                'Linear transformations warp the entire 2D coordinate space.',
                'Multiplying a matrix by a vector changes its position.',
                'See our Elastic-Cat stretch across the grid.',
                'Most vectors shift off their original path.',
                'They land on entirely new lines after transformation.'
            ]
        )

        # Colors
        PLANE_COLOR = "#1890FF"
        CAT_COLOR = "#FAAD14"
        VECTOR_COLOR = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FF4D4F"

        # Grid area constants
        GRID_CENTER = np.array([3.0, -0.3, 0])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Linear transformations warp the entire 2D coordinate space.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(PLANE_COLOR))
        
        # Create a local coordinate system in the grid area
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": PLANE_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": PLANE_COLOR},
        ).scale(0.7)
        plane.move_to(GRID_CENTER)
        
        self.play(Create(plane))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Multiplying a matrix by a vector changes its position.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(VECTOR_COLOR))
        
        # Create vectors relative to GRID_CENTER
        v_coords = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [-1, 1, 0]]
        vectors = VGroup(*[
            Arrow(
                start=GRID_CENTER,
                end=GRID_CENTER + plane.coords_to_point(c[0], c[1]) - plane.coords_to_point(0,0),
                buff=0,
                color=VECTOR_COLOR,
                stroke_width=4
            ) for c in v_coords
        ])
        
        # Original paths (dashed) to show "span" later
        spans = VGroup(*[
            DashedLine(
                GRID_CENTER - (plane.coords_to_point(c[0], c[1]) - plane.coords_to_point(0,0)) * 2,
                GRID_CENTER + (plane.coords_to_point(c[0], c[1]) - plane.coords_to_point(0,0)) * 2,
                color=WHITE,
                stroke_opacity=0.3
            ) for c in v_coords
        ])

        self.play(Create(vectors))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # See our Elastic-Cat stretch across the grid.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(CAT_COLOR))
        
        # Create a simple cat shape using lines
        cat_lines = VGroup(
            Line([-0.6, -0.4, 0], [0.6, -0.4, 0]), # bottom
            Line([-0.6, -0.4, 0], [-0.6, 0.4, 0]), # left
            Line([0.6, -0.4, 0], [0.6, 0.4, 0]),   # right
            Line([-0.6, 0.4, 0], [-0.2, 0.4, 0]),  # top-left
            Line([0.2, 0.4, 0], [0.6, 0.4, 0]),    # top-right
            Line([-0.2, 0.4, 0], [-0.4, 0.8, 0]),  # left-ear 1
            Line([-0.4, 0.8, 0], [0, 0.4, 0]),     # left-ear 2
            Line([0, 0.4, 0], [0.4, 0.8, 0]),      # right-ear 1
            Line([0.4, 0.8, 0], [0.2, 0.4, 0]),    # right-ear 2
        ).set_color(CAT_COLOR).scale(0.8)
        cat_lines.move_to(GRID_CENTER + UP * 0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(cat_lines))
        self.wait(1)

        # Apply transformation matrix [[1, 1], [0, 1]] (Shear)
        shear_matrix = [[1, 1, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
        
        # We transform the plane, cat, and vectors
        # Note: apply_matrix usually works about the origin. 
        # We need to apply it relative to GRID_CENTER.
        
        self.play(
            plane.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
            cat_lines.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
            vectors.animate.apply_matrix(shear_matrix, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Most vectors shift off their original path.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Show original spans to demonstrate the shift
        self.add_foreground_mobjects(vectors)
        self.play(FadeIn(spans))
        
        # Highlight vectors that are no longer on their dashed lines
        # Vector 1 [1,0] -> [1,0] (Stays on span)
        # Vector 2 [0,1] -> [1,1] (Shifts)
        # Vector 3 [-1,1] -> [0,1] (Shifts)
        self.play(
            vectors[1].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR),
            vectors[2].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR),
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # They land on entirely new lines after transformation.
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR))
        
        # Small pulsing effect on the shifted vectors to emphasize the change
        self.play(
            vectors[1].animate.scale(1.2, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
            vectors[2].animate.scale(1.2, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
        )
        self.play(
            vectors[1].animate.scale(1/1.2, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
            vectors[2].animate.scale(1/1.2, about_point=GRID_CENTER),
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x6 grid on right side)

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Data
        title_text = "Defining Eigenvectors: The Unchanging Directions"
        lecture_lines = [
            'Some special vectors stay on their original span.',
            'Watch the whisker as the cat stretches diagonally.',
            'It stays horizontal while everything else tilts.',
            'These unchanging directions are called eigenvectors.',
            "They define the transformation's fundamental axes."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        CAT_COLOR = "#FAAD14"
        PLANE_COLOR = "#1890FF"
        EIGEN_COLOR = "#52C41A"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = YELLOW

        # Reference center for transformations
        center_point = (self.grid["A1"] + self.grid["F6"]) / 2

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display the cat shape on the NumberPlane
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1], y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=6, y_length=6,
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": PLANE_COLOR, "stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        
        # Create a simple stylized cat face
        face = Circle(radius=0.6, color=CAT_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.2)
        left_ear = Polygon([-0.4, 0.4, 0], [-0.6, 0.9, 0], [-0.1, 0.6, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        right_ear = Polygon( [0.4, 0.4, 0], [0.6, 0.9, 0], [0.1, 0.6, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        # Whiskers - w2 is the horizontal one that will be the eigenvector
        w1 = Line([-0.3, 0.1, 0], [-0.9, 0.3, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        w2 = Line([-0.3, 0, 0], [-1.0, 0, 0], color=CAT_COLOR) 
        w3 = Line([-0.3, -0.1, 0], [-0.9, -0.3, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        w4 = Line([0.3, 0.1, 0], [0.9, 0.3, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        w5 = Line([0.3, 0, 0], [0.9, 0, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        w6 = Line([0.3, -0.1, 0], [0.9, -0.3, 0], color=CAT_COLOR)
        
        cat = VGroup(face, left_ear, right_ear, w1, w2, w3, w4, w5, w6)
        
        viz_group = VGroup(plane, cat)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, 'A1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane), FadeIn(cat))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Convert w2 into a prominent vector
        whisker_vector = Arrow(
            start=w2.get_start(),
            end=w2.get_end(),
            buff=0,
            color=EIGEN_COLOR,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(whisker_vector),
            w2.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Matrix to apply diagonal stretch/shear: [[2, 1], [0, 1]]
        matrix = [[2, 1], [0, 1]]
        
        # Transform the cat and the whisker vector centered at the cat's center
        self.play(
            cat.animate.apply_matrix(matrix, about_point=center_point),
            whisker_vector.animate.apply_matrix(matrix, about_point=center_point),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        v_start = whisker_vector.get_start()
        v_end = whisker_vector.get_end()
        v_dir = v_end - v_start
        v_dir_norm = v_dir / (np.linalg.norm(v_dir) + 1e-8)
        
        span_line = DashedLine(
            start=v_start - 4 * v_dir_norm,
            end=v_start + 2 * v_dir_norm,
            color=EIGEN_COLOR,
            stroke_width=2,
            dash_length=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(Create(span_line))
        self.add(whisker_vector)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        label = Text("Eigenvector", font_size=20, color=EIGEN_COLOR)
        self.place_at_grid(label, 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pointer = Arrow(
            start=label.get_bottom(),
            end=whisker_vector.get_center() + UP*0.1,
            buff=0.1,
            color=EIGEN_COLOR,
            stroke_width=3,
            max_tip_length_to_length_ratio=0.15
        )
        
        self.play(Write(label), GrowArrow(pointer))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        title_text = "Defining Eigenvalues: The Scale of Change"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Eigenvalues measure how much eigenvectors stretch or shrink.",
            "If the whisker triples in length, lambda is three.",
            "Negative values mean the vector flips direction."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # Vector styling
        EIGENVECTOR_COLOR = "#52C41A"
        SCALAR_COLOR = "#F5222D"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Line 1: Eigenvalues measure how much eigenvectors stretch or shrink.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Base eigenvector (unit length)
        # Using grid points: D2 is x=1.5, D3 is x=2.5. Vector points from D2 to D3 (length 1).
        v_start = self.grid["D2"]
        v_end_1 = self.grid["D3"]
        vec = Arrow(v_start, v_end_1, color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Labeling the vector with Text "v"
        vec_label = Text("v", color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, font_size=24, slant=ITALIC)
        self.place_at_grid(vec_label, "E2", scale_factor=0.8) # Positioned near start
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(vec), FadeIn(vec_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Line 2: If the whisker triples in length, lambda is three.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Scale the vector from length 1 to length 3
        # D2 is x=1.5. D5 is x=4.5. Distance = 3.0.
        v_end_3 = self.grid["D5"]
        vec_3 = Arrow(v_start, v_end_3, color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Label λ = 3 (Using Unicode Lambda)
        lambda_3_label = Text("λ = 3", color=SCALAR_COLOR, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(lambda_3_label, "C4")
        
        # Equation Av = 3v constructed via Text VGroup
        eq_parts = VGroup(
            Text("A", color=WHITE, font_size=28, weight=BOLD),
            Text("v", color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, font_size=28, slant=ITALIC),
            Text(" = ", color=WHITE, font_size=28),
            Text("3", color=SCALAR_COLOR, font_size=32),
            Text("v", color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, font_size=28, slant=ITALIC)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_parts, "B4")
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(vec, vec_3),
            FadeIn(lambda_3_label),
            FadeIn(eq_parts)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Line 3: Negative values mean the vector flips direction.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Flip the vector: Point to x=0.5 (D1). Start is x=1.5 (D2). Length is 1, but flipped.
        v_end_neg = self.grid["D1"]
        vec_neg = Arrow(v_start, v_end_neg, color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, buff=0, stroke_width=6)
        
        # Label λ = -1
        lambda_neg_label = Text("λ = -1", color=SCALAR_COLOR, font_size=32)
        self.place_at_grid(lambda_neg_label, "C1")
        
        # Update equation to Av = -1v
        eq_neg_parts = VGroup(
            Text("A", color=WHITE, font_size=28, weight=BOLD),
            Text("v", color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, font_size=28, slant=ITALIC),
            Text(" = ", color=WHITE, font_size=28),
            Text("-1", color=SCALAR_COLOR, font_size=32),
            Text("v", color=EIGENVECTOR_COLOR, font_size=28, slant=ITALIC)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_neg_parts, "B1")
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(vec_3, vec_neg),
            ReplacementTransform(lambda_3_label, lambda_neg_label),
            ReplacementTransform(eq_parts, eq_neg_parts)
        )
        self.wait(3)

        # Reset final color
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(1)

        # Create tilted grid lines
        tilted_grid = VGroup()
        for i in range(-3, 4):
            # Lines parallel to v1
            start1 = i * v2 - 2.5 * v1
            end1 = i * v2 + 2.5 * v1
            line1 = Line(start1, end1, stroke_width=1, stroke_opacity=0.4, color=GRID_COLOR)
            tilted_grid.add(line1)
            
            # Lines parallel to v2

outline.topic: Decoding the DNA of Linear Transformations: Eigenvectors, Eigenvalues, and Eigenbasis
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM or advanced high school students with a background in basic matrix multiplication.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Linear Transformations as Space Warping
sections.content: Introduce the concept that multiplying a vector by a matrix 'transforms' space. Use a 2D grid to show how space can stretch, rotate, or shear. Explain that most vectors knock off their original span (line) during this transformation.
sections.example: Visualize a character named 'Elastic-Cat' on a 2D coordinate plane. When a matrix is applied, the cat stretches diagonally. Most points on the cat move to entirely new directions relative to the origin.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvectors: The Unchanging Directions
sections.content: Define an eigenvector as a special vector that stays on its own span after the transformation. While the rest of the world rotates or tilts, these vectors only get longer, shorter, or flip direction—they never leave their original line.
sections.example: In the 'Elastic-Cat' stretch, notice a specific whisker pointing exactly along the X-axis. Even as the cat grows larger, that whisker stays perfectly horizontal. That whisker is an eigenvector.

sections.title: Defining Eigenvalues: The Scale of Change
sections.content: Introduce the eigenvalue (λ). It is the scalar factor by which the eigenvector is stretched or compressed. If λ > 1, it stretches; if 0 < λ < 1, it shrinks; if λ is negative, it flips direction.
sections.example: If the 'Horizontal Whisker' (eigenvector) was 1 unit long and becomes 3 units long after the transformation, the eigenvalue λ equals 3. If it stayed the same length, λ would be 1.

sections.title: The Characteristic Equation: Finding the Secret Directions
sections.content: Transition to the mathematical representation: Av = λv. Explain that we solve det(A - λI) = 0 to find the eigenvalues, and then find the null space to get the eigenvectors. Use a geometric intuition for 'determinant equals zero' (collapsing space).
sections.example: Show a 2x2 matrix A. Through an animation, subtract λ from the diagonal, showing how changing λ 'squashes' the transformation until it flattens space into a line—this specific λ is our eigenvalue.

sections.title: The Eigenbasis: A Better Point of View
sections.content: Explain that if we have enough eigenvectors, we can use them as a new coordinate system (a basis). In this 'Eigenbasis,' the complex matrix transformation becomes a simple diagonal matrix, making calculations like 'Matrix Power' (A^n) incredibly easy.
sections.example: Imagine a bird flying diagonally. Instead of describing its movement using awkward X and Y coordinates, we tilt our entire coordinate grid to align with the bird's path and its wings. This 'tilted grid' is the Eigenbasis, making the bird's flight math simple.

sections.title: Real-world Application & Summary
sections.content: Summarize the flow: Matrix -> Eigenvectors (Directions) -> Eigenvalues (Magnitude) -> Eigenbasis (Simplified Worldview). Mention real-world usage like PageRank (Google) or Facial Recognition (Eigenfaces).
sections.example: Show how 'Eigenfaces' uses these concepts to identify the most important features in a human face, ignoring the noise and focusing on the primary 'directions' of facial variance.

storyboard.title: The Eigenbasis: A Better Point of View
lecture_lines: Eigenvectors can form a natural coordinate system.
In this Eigenbasis, transformations only scale vectors.
This turns complex matrices into simple diagonal ones.
We decompose the matrix using these fundamental directions.
Now, calculating high matrix powers becomes instant scaling.
animations: Construct a new coordinate grid (#52C41A) using two eigenvectors as the basis vectors.
Transform a vector (#FAAD14) on this grid, showing it only scales along the new axes.
Display a diagonal matrix D (#FFFFFF) with eigenvalues on the main diagonal.
Show the matrix decomposition equation 'A = PDP⁻¹' (#FFFFFF) with 'D' highlighted.
Animate 'A^10' by showing the basis vectors scaling by 'λ^10' (#F5222D) instantly.

storyboard.title: Real-world Application & Summary
lecture_lines: Eigenvectors reveal the core DNA of transformations.
They power Google's search and facial recognition systems.
Understanding them unlocks the heart of linear algebra.
animations: Display a summary flow chart: Matrix → Eigenvectors (#52C41A) → Eigenvalues (#F5222D).
Show a facial outline [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/face.svg] (#FAAD14) with arrows indicating primary 'directions' of facial features (Eigenfaces).
Fade in the final title: 'The DNA of Linear Transformations' (#FFFFFF) centered on screen.
